derivation_steps.content: A rigid block of mass $m = 5\text{ kg}$ is displaced along the horizontal $+x$-axis under a constant pulling force $\vec{F}$ inclined at angle $\theta = 60^\circ$ above the horizontal.

derivation_steps.title: Represent the Coordinate System & Vectors
derivation_steps.content: Establish Cartesian coordinates with $+x$ pointing horizontally rightward along displacement $\vec{d} = 10\hat{i}\text{ m}$ and $+y$ pointing vertically upward. derivation_steps.content: By the scalar work definition for constant forces: $W = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{d} = F_x d_x + F_y d_y = (F \cos\theta)(d) + (F \sin\theta)(0) = F d \cos\theta$.

derivation_steps.title: Execute Exact Calculation
derivation_steps.content: Substitute numerical values: $W = (40\text{ N})(10\text{ m})\cos 60^\circ = 400 \times 0.5 = 200\text{ J}$.

derivation_steps.title: Interpret Final Result & Units
derivation_steps.content: The applied force transfers $200\text{ J}$ of energy to the block. Exactly half of the force magnitude contributes to horizontal acceleration, while the perpendicular component reduces normal contact force without transferring energy.

derivation_steps.title: Understand the Physical Regime
derivation_steps.content: A satellite executes uniform circular motion around Earth. The only force acting is gravity, which supplies the necessary centripetal acceleration toward the Earth's center.

derivation_steps.title: Represent Orthogonal Vector Directions
derivation_steps.content: In polar coordinates $(r, \theta)$, the gravitational force is purely radial: $\vec{F}_g = -\frac{G M m}{R^2} \hat{r}$. The instantaneous displacement is purely tangential: $d\vec{r} = R\,d\theta\,\hat{\theta}$.

derivation_steps.title: Connect Work Line Integral
derivation_steps.content: The incremental work done during displacement $d\vec{r}$ is $dW = \vec{F}_g \cdot d\vec{r} = \left(-\frac{G M m}{R^2} \hat{r}\right) \cdot (R\,d\theta\,\hat{\theta})$. Since $\hat{r} \cdot \hat{\theta} = 0$, $dW = 0$ at every instant.

derivation_steps.title: Execute Path Integration
derivation_steps.content: Integrate around one complete circular orbit: $W = \oint \vec{F}_g \cdot d\vec{r} = \int_0^{2\pi} 0 \cdot R\,d\theta = 0\text{ J}$.

derivation_steps.title: Interpret Final Invariant
derivation_steps.content: Because centripetal forces are perpendicular to velocity, they alter direction without changing speed or kinetic energy. Consequently, planets and satellites remain in stable circular orbits indefinitely without energy dissipation.

derivation_steps.content: The particle oscillates back and forth in the potential trough between $x = 4.0\text{ m}$ and an inner turning point near $x = 1.0\text{ m}$, attaining peak speed $2.0\text{ m/s}$ as it glides through $x = 3.0\text{ m}$.

derivation_steps.title: Understand the Physical Regime
derivation_steps.content: A particle moves in a 1D molecular-type potential well $U(x) = \frac{a}{x^2} - \frac{b}{x}$. The binding energy is the minimum energy required to detach the particle from its potential well to infinity.

derivation_steps.title: Represent Equilibrium Force Condition
derivation_steps.content: At equilibrium, conservative force vanishes: $F(x) = -\frac{dU}{dx} = 0$.

derivation_steps.title: Connect Calculus Extremum
derivation_steps.content: Differentiate $U(x)$ with respect to $x$: $\frac{dU}{dx} = -\frac{2a}{x^3} + \frac{b}{x^2} = \frac{b x - 2a}{x^3} = 0$. This yields the unique equilibrium separation $x_0 = \frac{2a}{b}$.

derivation_steps.title: Execute Potential Well Depth Calculation

derivation_steps.title: Interpret Binding Energy
derivation_steps.content: Since $U(\infty) = 0$, the binding energy is $E_b = U(\infty) - U(x_0) = 0 - \left(-\frac{b^2}{4a}\right) = \frac{b^2}{4a}$. Supplying energy $E_b$ elevates the particle from the potential well to free ionization.
